title: God judges the dead by the desires of their hearts
Christ organized the righteous dead to preach to all spirits
The Church ends the public practice of plural marriage
setting: In the 1880s, federal laws made plural marriage a crime and targeted the Church’s property. The Edmunds-Tucker Act of 1887 disincorporated the Church and allowed seizure of its assets. Many Church leaders were jailed or went into hiding, and temples were at risk. In 1890 the Supreme Court upheld the seizure law. President Wilford Woodruff issued this statement on 24 September 1890.
summary: This is an official statement, often called the Manifesto, issued by President Wilford Woodruff. It denies reports that the Church was still teaching or performing plural marriages. Woodruff says he will submit to the federal laws against plural marriage and urges members to do the same. On 6 October 1890, general conference voted to accept it as authoritative and binding. Excerpts from three of Woodruff’s later addresses follow it. In them he says the Lord showed him that, without the change, temple work would stop and leaders would be jailed.
lds: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson “We Believe”: Articles of Faith and Official Declarations 1 and 2 asks what Woodruff’s reasons teach about God’s work. In the 1891 excerpt, what two outcomes does Woodruff ask members to weigh, and why does he say the change was needed?

title: Priesthood and temple blessings are extended to all worthy members
setting: A few Black men were ordained to the priesthood in the Church’s early years, including Elijah Abel. In 1852 Brigham Young announced that men of Black African descent could not be ordained. Black men and women were also kept from temple endowments and sealings. Church records give no clear origin for the practice, and the Church now disavows past theories offered to explain it. The issue grew pressing in the 1970s, as the Church grew in Brazil and West Africa.
summary: This is a letter from the First Presidency announcing a revelation, dated 8 June 1978. It was signed by Spencer W. Kimball and his counselors, N. Eldon Tanner and Marion G. Romney. It reports that they prayed at length in the Upper Room of the Salt Lake Temple. They say a revelation confirmed that all worthy men may be ordained, without regard for race or color. The letter extends temple blessings with the priesthood, so worthy men may share them with their families. Local leaders are to interview each candidate for worthiness as usual. On 30 September 1978, general conference voted unanimously to accept it as the word and will of the Lord.
lds: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson on Official Declarations 1 and 2, “We Believe,” says the restriction’s reason is not known. How does the letter’s stated aim of extending every blessing to every worthy member connect with 2 Nephi 26:33?
